prompt: We store encrypted PII with envelope encryption: every row carries its own DEK, and that DEK is stored wrapped by Vault's Transit engine under a master key. Reading a field means unwrapping the DEK via Vault, then AES-decrypting the ciphertext locally. Profiling the read path shows Vault dominating: every single-record decrypt does a full HTTP round-trip to unwrap its DEK — even seconds after the same record was just read — and the batch/list endpoint that loads N records fires N separate unwrap calls against Vault. On top of that, our Vault client points at one instance, so a Vault blip or failover takes down every read. Given the code below, how would you optimize this hot path without weakening the security guarantees envelope encryption exists to give us — bounded blast radius per DEK and the ability to crypto-shred by destroying a key?
